title: Research to Reality: Bringing Frontier ML Research to Production - Vaidas Razgaitis, Higharc
talk_summary: A senior research engineer at Higharc describes how they hand off ML research prototypes to production software engineers using three levers: a structured 'research prototype taxonomy' design doc, a decoupled microservice monorepo with consistent layered skeletons, and a deliberate PR decomposition/review plan using stacked diffs (Graphite).

takeaways.technique: Mandatory structured handoff doc before build
takeaways.what_they_do: Every research prototype must produce a 'research prototype taxonomy' document (domain context/lingo, business goal, type contracts, persistence layer, system architecture, decomposition plan) before engineers touch it, so newcomers know exactly where to concentrate effort.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have a very analogous document um that we require from all research prototypes that we call the research prototype taxonomy document

takeaways.what_they_do: They keep a separate ML monorepo of fully decoupled microservices with a one-to-one researcher-to-microservice ratio and a gateway routing requests, so each initiative can iterate independently.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's pretty much a one-to-one researcher to microservice ratio. So, we find that works really well.

takeaways.technique: Consistent skeletal repo layout for agent navigation
takeaways.what_they_do: Each microservice uses the same layered skeleton (API/controller/service/data) with cleanly documented specs and root-level metadata/Dockerfile/lockfiles so agents can navigate repos predictably.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we tend to have like some really um really cleanly documented specs uh so that agents can navigate these repositories

takeaways.technique: Stacked-diff decomposition with targeted SME review
takeaways.what_they_do: They slice monolithic prototypes along dependency-graph axes into stacked PRs (Graphite) enabling asynchronous review, then route each small slice to the specific subject-matter expert who should review it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we use Graphite um for kind of stack diffs to then uh decompose these large monolithic prototypes

takeaways.technique: Decomposition plan derived from the design doc
takeaways.what_they_do: The taxonomy doc's architecture/persistence/type sections directly inform the decomposition strategy, so slicing is planned up front rather than improvised.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that tends to inform uh your decomposition strategy on how to bring it into the into the mono repo

takeaways.what_they_do: They use three diagnostic questions (is it obvious where staff should focus? are there templates/patterns to mimic? can you consistently estimate timelines and pick reviewers?) to detect process or repo problems.
takeaways.evidence_quote: are you able to consistently estimate the timelines and delivery dates for moving research concepts into your repository?
